descriptor.scene: NOBODY IS IN THIS PICTURE: no figures, no hands, no faces. The engine alone is the subject, quiet on the green in the deep gold of dusk, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the waist-high rounded cream machine on its low base, its one great dial upright on top, the single bold needle standing exactly UPRIGHT at mid-dial between the small snail mark at the left end and the small winged-block mark at the right end. Calm, even warm hum lines rise gently off its body into the evening air. The dusk light turns its cream to warm gold; long soft shadows lie on the grass; far behind it, the small warm lights of the built plain glow under a rose-and-gold sky. Peaceful, certain, ongoing. The lower right of the frame stays calm dusk grass, open and quiet for the closing words.
negatives: any figure, hand or face in frame
the needle leaning left or right (exactly upright)
numbers, tick marks or lettering on the dial
darkness or gloom (dusk is warm gold, never cold)
descriptor._caption: The engines can go a million miles an hour. The founders who last go just right. Too hot burns. Too cold starves. Just right compounds.

prompt: Picture-book spread painted in the warm editorial ink-and-wash register of the FIRST reference image. THE FIRST REFERENCE IMAGE IS A STYLE ANCHOR ONLY. Match it for MEDIUM, BRUSHWORK, PALETTE and LIGHT QUALITY ONLY, and take NO subject from it whatsoever: none of its objects, figures, costume, props, furniture, architecture, period or location may appear in the output unless the scene description below asks for them by name. SCENE: NOBODY IS IN THIS PICTURE: no figures, no hands, no faces. The engine alone is the subject, quiet on the green in the deep gold of dusk, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the waist-high rounded cream machine on its low base, its one great dial upright on top, the single bold needle standing exactly UPRIGHT at mid-dial between the small snail mark at the left end and the small winged-block mark at the right end. Calm, even warm hum lines rise gently off its body into the evening air. The dusk light turns its cream to warm gold; long soft shadows lie on the grass; far behind it, the small warm lights of the built plain glow under a rose-and-gold sky. Peaceful, certain, ongoing. The lower right of the frame stays calm dusk grass, open and quiet for the closing words. THE CAMERA MOVES; NOTHING ELSE DOES. Every person keeps the exact seat, side and place the setting's blocking gives them, and if a BLOCKING PLATE is supplied it is the authority on who sits where: obey it at every distance. Whatever the subject is sitting at, leaning on or standing beside is STILL IN THIS PICTURE, in the near foreground if the camera is close. Everyone else present in this place is STILL PRESENT in the picture, behind or beside the subject, soft and out of focus if they are not the subject, and NOBODY leaves and NO seat empties because the camera came closer. FRAMING, IMAGINED: this picture shows the THING BEING DESCRIBED, full bleed, and the people describing it are NOT in the frame at all. Nobody listens, nobody speaks, and no part of the room the conversation happens in appears. Paint the idea itself as a real place or a real object, in the same register as the rest of the book, with no bubble, no border, no vignette and no lettering. the-pace-engine exactly as its reference plate: The identical machine every founder receives on the far side of the portal: a waist-high rounded machine body in flat cream, resting on a low base, with ONE large circular dial on its top and nothing else. The dial carries a single bold needle. At the dial's left end sits a small snail mark; at the dial's right end sits a small winged-block mark (the deck's dial glyphs, a cross-artifact echo of takeoffwithclaude.com's Goldilocks-pace slide). The engine can run at any speed; the dial is the only control it has. The machine itself never differs between founders and never changes between states: only the needle's position, the glow, and what the engine is putting out change. Proportions are pinned as numbers and shared by every state. The machine stands waist-high to an adult figure: body 0.95 m tall on a 0.10 m base (about 1.05 m overall against a 1.7 m adult). The body is 1.0 m wide; the dial's diameter is 0.5 m, roughly HALF the body width, standing upright and centered on the top of the body, its face toward the viewer so it reads like a gauge (locked in the blessed master, 2026-08-09). The needle pivots from the dial's center: upright at mid-dial in the steady state, hard right in roar, hard left in cold. The snail mark sits at the left end of the dial's arc, the winged-block mark at the right end; each glyph is small, about one-eighth of the dial's diameter. In frame the engine sits on the ground plane, whole and unobstructed enough that the dial and both glyphs stay legible. Ink outlines with flat cream fills (warm cream body, slightly deeper cream base), terracotta-compatible accents; the needle and the two dial glyphs are drawn in ink. State-dependent only: steady adds calm, even warm hum lines rising gently off the body; roar adds a hot glow around the engine and motion blur in its output; cold shows the engine dark and untouched, its cream dimmed toward dusk with NO glow and no hum lines. Never neon, never HUD chrome, never glossy plastic, never 3D render sheen. Waist-high to an adult: the top of the machine body reaches an adult's waist, and the dial on top sits about hip-to-navel height. In a wide shot it reads as a generous household-appliance-sized machine a founder stands beside, never a room-sized turbine and never a handheld gadget. THERE ARE NO PEOPLE AND NO CHARACTERS OF ANY KIND IN THIS IMAGE. No person, no figure, no head, no shoulder, no arm, no hand, no silhouette, no reflection of a person, and nobody seated in any chair. Any place a figure might be expected is empty. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, any figure, hand or face in frame, the needle leaning left or right (exactly upright), numbers, tick marks or lettering on the dial, more than one engine, darkness or gloom (dusk is warm gold, never cold). ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. If a person in this scene is moving toward something, that destination MUST BE AHEAD OF THEM IN THE FRAME and they must be seen FROM BEHIND or from three-quarters behind, so the viewer is following them into it. A figure whose face is toward the camera is walking AWAY from everything behind them: if the thing they are moving toward is drawn behind them, the picture says the opposite of the scene. Their feet, hips, shoulders and gaze all point the same way, along the direction of travel. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
